● Industry news · 4 min read

⚡ Insurance compliance is on the trades tech map. It's filed under getting paid.

Suffolk Technologies just mapped the tools reshaping how trade contractors win, run, do and get paid for work. Insurance compliance made the map, in the last column. Where it sits says a lot about how the industry still treats it.

✅ Suffolk Technologies' November 2026 map groups emerging tools for trade contractors into five stages: win and staff work, run the business, plan and coordinate work, do the work, and get paid and manage cash.

✅ Insurance compliance is on it, filed under payment compliance in the get paid stage, next to pay apps and lien waivers.

● COI basics · 5 min read

✅ What does per project aggregate mean on a contractor COI?

It means your project gets its own general aggregate limit instead of sharing one with every job the contractor works that year. A per project aggregate comes from an endorsement such as CG 25 03, and the certificate's PRO-JECT box only summarizes it. Completed operations claims still share a separate aggregate.

✅ Per project aggregate means the contractor's general aggregate limit applies separately to each designated construction project, instead of one limit shared by all of its work.

✅ Without it, claims paid on the contractor's other jobs during the policy year reduce the same aggregate that's supposed to protect your project.

● Market outlook · 2 min read

☂️ Contractor backlog fell to 8.1 months. What it means for COIs

Backlog fell sharply in October, and the drop was concentrated among contractors without data center work. Thinner pipelines change who bids on your jobs.

✅ ABC's Construction Backlog Indicator fell to 8.1 months in October 2026, down 0.6 months from September and 0.3 months from a year earlier.

✅ The drop came from contractors without data center work. Their backlog fell from 8.3 to 7.6 months, while contractors with data center work rose from 11.3 to 11.5 months.

● Buyer's guide · 16 min read

✏️ Best COI tracking software for construction (2026): 8 tools compared

What each tool checks on a subcontractor COI, who fixes the gap, whether it connects to Procore, and what it costs, from Forsured, Billy, bcs, Jones, PINS Advantage, TrustLayer, illumend and Certificial.

✅ All eight tools look at endorsements, not just the ACORD 25 certificate. They differ in how deep the review goes, who makes the final call, and how the broker gets the fix back to you. That's where the best COI tracking software for your company gets decided.

✅ Forsured is built around requirements that change by project and a shared workspace where the broker sees what's missing. PINS Advantage goes deepest on endorsement wording inside Procore. bcs publishes per-vendor rates and has a free tier. Certificial gets live policy data from the agent.

● Buyer's guide · 8 min read

✏️ Which COI tracking software checks endorsements, not just certificates?

Almost every COI tracking tool now says it checks endorsements. What differs is how far it reads: the form type, a list of required forms, the wording, or the full policy. Here's where eight tools land, from their own pages.

✅ Most COI tracking software for construction now checks endorsements, not just certificates. The real difference is depth: naming the endorsement type, flagging missing required forms, reading the wording against your requirements, or reading the full policy.

✅ On their own pages, Forsured, PINS Advantage, TrustLayer and illumend describe reading the endorsement wording. Billy flags missing required forms such as CG 20 10, CG 20 37, waiver of subrogation and primary and noncontributory. bcs and Certificial describe identifying the endorsement and pulling its key fields.
